title: Lapatinib + capecitabine

agents.name: Lapatinib
agents.explanation: Lapatinib inhibits HER2 and EGFR signalling inside cancer cells. It is used with capecitabine in selected previously treated HER2-positive advanced breast cancer.
agents.watch: Report new or worsening symptoms promptly and follow the agreed contact plan.

agents.name: Capecitabine
agents.explanation: The body converts capecitabine into fluorouracil, which disrupts DNA and RNA processes needed for cell growth. Tablets are active chemotherapy; taking them at home still requires a clear monitoring and interruption plan.
agents.watch: Stop tablets and contact the team for significant diarrhoea, painful mouth ulcers, hand-foot soreness affecting activities, fever or dehydration. Chest pain needs urgent assessment. Do not restart until instructed.
risks: Severe early toxicity including DPD-related toxicity

context_label: HER2-positive advanced breast cancer · previously treated
purpose: Control the cancer and symptoms, with repeated review of benefit and tolerance.
schedule_summary: Lapatinib once daily on Days 1–21, continuously. Capecitabine twice daily on Days 1–14, then no capecitabine on Days 15–21. Repeat every 21 days while beneficial and tolerated. The capecitabine rest week is not a lapatinib rest week.

phases_title: The phases and how they connect
phases_note: Relative sequence, not equal lengths or booked dates. Your team confirms actual appointments and the active medicines.
timeline_note: Treatment markers show the planned schedule. Symptom bands are broad possibilities, not measured risk curves; serious symptoms can occur at any time.
safety_note: Serious symptoms need assessment on any day, even if the chart shows a usual recovery period.
teachback: Which medicines are active now, which days do you receive or take them, and who is booking and reviewing your next tests?
consent_support: Discuss the treatment aim, alternatives, expected benefit, common and serious effects, fertility and pregnancy precautions, route, monitoring, practical support and the agreed contact plan. The treating team completes the approved individual consent process.
urgent_extra: Report new breathlessness, chest symptoms, severe diarrhoea, dehydration, jaundice, unusual bleeding or sudden illness promptly. Do not wait for the next planned test.

support.title: A clear tablet schedule
support.text: Take lapatinib at least one hour before or after food, consistently in the same relation to meals. Take capecitabine with food or within 30 minutes after eating. Swallow tablets whole. A pharmacist can help arrange the different food timings.

support.title: Nausea and bowel plan
support.text: These oral agents are classified as minimal-to-low emetic risk. Agree an individual symptom plan; a repeated IV chemotherapy antiemetic course is not automatically required.

support.title: Early symptoms matter
support.text: Call promptly for diarrhoea, dehydration, painful hands or feet, mouth ulcers or poor intake. New chest pain needs urgent assessment.

support.title: Before restarting a cycle
support.text: Review bloods, kidney and liver function, symptoms and the agreed doses. Do not restart tablets after a treatment hold without the team’s instructions.

questions.a: Ask the team who books each test, who checks the result and who to contact if an appointment is overdue. This map does not book appointments.

questions.q: What if I become unwell between visits?
questions.a: Use the urgent contact plan for sudden illness, fever, chest symptoms, severe diarrhoea or poor fluid intake. Do not wait for a scheduled blood test or scan.

This all-tablet combination may be considered when HER2-positive advanced cancer has progressed after previous treatment including an anthracycline, a taxane and trastuzumab in the metastatic setting. It blocks growth signals and uses chemotherapy through a different mechanism. Earlier medicines, cancer sites, kidney and liver health, tolerance and available alternatives affect the choice.

questions.q: When is my next heart scan?
questions.a: NCCP requires baseline LVEF assessment in its cardiac precautions and echo/MUGA every 12 weeks (around cycle 5 if on time), or earlier for concern. EMA Tyverb specifies an ECG with QT before starting and again 1–2 weeks after starting, around Days 8–15 of cycle 1. Correct low potassium or magnesium before treatment and arrange extra ECG checks for interacting medicines, symptoms or QT risk. This early ECG is separate from the 12-week echo.

Surgery or radiotherapy may be used for particular symptoms or disease sites. There is no routine surgery-then-radiation sequence for this advanced-cancer regimen. The oncology and radiation teams agree any treatment pause or overlap.

questions.q: Do I need regular scans or markers?
questions.a: Record baseline disease sites. Response imaging is generally reviewed every 2–4 months under international guidance, adapted to symptoms, disease pace and treatment. The team selects the scan; this is not an automatic CT chest/abdomen/pelvis order for every patient. Tumour markers may support assessment in selected cases, but do not alone decide progression or a treatment change.

questions.q: Does the rest week apply to both medicines?
questions.a: No. Days 15–21 are a capecitabine break; lapatinib continues each day unless your team tells you to hold it.

items.title: Schedule

chapters.title: Two tablets, two different schedules
chapters.intro: Lapatinib once daily on Days 1–21, continuously. Capecitabine twice daily on Days 1–14, then no capecitabine on Days 15–21. Repeat every 21 days while beneficial and tolerated. The capecitabine rest week is not a lapatinib rest week.

items.title: Food timing
items.text: Take lapatinib at least one hour before or after food, consistently in the same relation to meals. Take capecitabine with food or within 30 minutes after eating. Swallow tablets whole. A pharmacist can help arrange the different food timings.

items.title: Medicines review
items.text: Check all prescription, over-the-counter and herbal medicines with the oncology pharmacist. Acid-reducing medicines can affect lapatinib absorption: NCCP specifies separation by at least two hours, while the product information cautions against acid-suppressing combinations. Do not start or stop a necessary acid medicine yourself; agree a plan. Avoid grapefruit and report any recent brivudine use.

items.title: Missed dose or vomiting
items.text: Do not double up or replace a vomited lapatinib dose. Follow the written missed-dose plan and contact the team if unsure. Significant diarrhoea, painful hands/feet, mouth ulcers or inability to drink may require tablets to be paused: call promptly for instructions.

items.title: Before first capecitabine
items.text: DPD testing must be reviewed before starting capecitabine unless already tested. The result can change the plan. Testing does not remove the need to report early or severe side effects.

chapters.title: When scans, heart checks and bloods happen
chapters.intro: Agree who books each test, who reviews the result and what happens if a check is overdue.

items.title: Blood tests
items.text: FBC, kidney and liver profile at baseline and before every 21-day cycle. The team reviews the necessary results before a planned dose.

items.title: Heart ultrasound and ECG
items.text: NCCP requires baseline LVEF assessment in its cardiac precautions and echo/MUGA every 12 weeks (around cycle 5 if on time), or earlier for concern. EMA Tyverb specifies an ECG with QT before starting and again 1–2 weeks after starting, around Days 8–15 of cycle 1. Correct low potassium or magnesium before treatment and arrange extra ECG checks for interacting medicines, symptoms or QT risk. This early ECG is separate from the 12-week echo.

items.title: Scans and tumour markers
items.text: Record baseline disease sites. Response imaging is generally reviewed every 2–4 months under international guidance, adapted to symptoms, disease pace and treatment. The team selects the scan; this is not an automatic CT chest/abdomen/pelvis order for every patient. Tumour markers may support assessment in selected cases, but do not alone decide progression or a treatment change.

items.title: Bone health and endocrine treatment
items.text: If the cancer is also hormone-receptor positive, endocrine treatment may form part of the wider plan. Bone-density testing is linked to aromatase inhibitors, ovarian suppression and fracture risk; it is not automatically required because a HER2 medicine is prescribed. Agree baseline DEXA where indicated and individual follow-up.

logistics.title: Your practical tablet plan
logistics.intro: Both anticancer medicines are taken by mouth. This regimen itself requires no infusion pump or port.

steps.title: Before starting
steps.text: Confirm DPD result, blood tests, cardiac assessment, medicines review and the two tablet schedules.

steps.title: Collect and check the prescription
steps.text: Confirm tablet strengths, doses, Days 1–14 for capecitabine and continuous lapatinib. Keep in the original packaging and out of reach of children.

steps.title: Food and medicine timing
steps.text: Take lapatinib at least one hour before or after food, consistently in the same relation to meals. Take capecitabine with food or within 30 minutes after eating. Swallow tablets whole. A pharmacist can help arrange the different food timings.

steps.title: Before each new cycle
steps.text: Keep blood and clinical-review appointments even though treatment is at home. Bring your medicine list and tell the team about missed or held doses.

details.title: Interactions
details.text: Check all prescription, over-the-counter and herbal medicines with the oncology pharmacist. Acid-reducing medicines can affect lapatinib absorption: NCCP specifies separation by at least two hours, while the product information cautions against acid-suppressing combinations. Do not start or stop a necessary acid medicine yourself; agree a plan. Avoid grapefruit and report any recent brivudine use.

details.title: Missed or vomited tablets
details.text: Do not make up or double a dose. Follow the written instructions and call if unsure.

details.title: If you already have a port
details.text: Ask the line team whether it is still needed and how it should be maintained or removed. Removal is a separate planned procedure.

anatomy: Report diarrhoea early, especially dizziness, poor intake or reduced urine.
Painful redness or peeling affecting activity needs prompt advice.
Report yellow skin or eyes, dark urine or severe itching.
New chest pain, breathlessness, palpitations or swelling needs urgent assessment.
Ulcers or difficulty eating and drinking need advice.
Report widespread rash, blistering or fever promptly.
anatomy_note: The map shows selected effects of the medicines named here. Report persistent effects from earlier treatment too.
